passages.context: Read visually in Friedberg I, column 1188, and checked against the exact MDZ c.88 transcription response. Section 1 directs the penitent seeking grace to 'querat sacerdotem scientem ligare et soluere.' Section 2 treats inability to reach a priest: 'si deest sacerdos, confiteatur proximo'; it immediately denies the neighbor the power of loosing and grounds the penitent's worthiness for pardon in 'desiderio sacerdotis.' It then invokes the lepers who were cleansed while going to show themselves to the priests: 'Mundati enim sunt leprosi, dum ibant ostendere ora sacerdotibus ante, quam ad eos peruenirent. Unde patet, Deum ad cor respicere, dum ex necessitate prohibentur ad sacerdotes peruenire.'
passages.notes: The exact MDZ chapter response for dc_chapter_3_3490 was also acquired on 2026-08-21 (SHA-256 e5c509164dc4e64a6551feeec2309dee351b01adc702ba46c6f3ba0132562c6f, 8,997 bytes); its LF physical lines 65-86 contain sections 1-2. This passage supports personal confession to a priest and a necessity case in which confession to a neighbor manifests desire for the unavailable priest. It does not give the neighbor sacramental power to absolve; the text expressly says he lacks 'potestatem soluendi.' Friedberg's preceding dictum introduces c.88 as an authority of Augustine from a book De penitentia; this record establishes Friedberg's received attribution and wording, not modern critical authorship of that work.

passages.context: Read visually in Friedberg I, columns 1165-1166, and checked against the exact MDZ c.34 transcription response. The dictum begins '[Gratian.] Conuersio autem dicitur quasi cordis undique uersio.' In section 1 it states: 'Dominus ostenderet, quod non sacerdotali iudicio, sed largitate diuinae gratiae peccator emundatur'; it then distinguishes the acts without suppressing either: 'Leprosus semetipsum sacerdoti representat, dum peccatum suum sacerdoti penitens confitetur. Sacrificium offert ex lege, dum satisfactionem ecclesiae iudicio sibi inpositam factis exequitur. Sed ante, quam ad sacerdotes perueniat, emundatur, dum per contritionem cordis ante confessionem oris peccati uenia indulgetur.' Section 2 continues the resurrection image: one raised by the Lord lives while confessing and has the raiser present and indwelling.
passages.notes: The exact MDZ chapter response for dc_chapter_3_3436 was also acquired on 2026-08-21 (SHA-256 e4b376bf6ec4f1103d9db6a89d1bb0960900b04f42c2d0eb1bdfdee8f4edff86, 7,477 bytes); its LF physical lines 24-80 carry the dictum, with the controlling contrast and its confession/satisfaction development at lines 38-54. This passage establishes the argument made at this stage of Gratian's dialectical treatment: cleansing and pardon are attributed to divine grace through inward contrition before oral confession, while personal confession to the priest and satisfaction imposed by ecclesial judgment remain real subsequent acts. It does not by itself establish the final disposition of the whole quaestio; the later dictum post c.87 expressly reinterprets earlier contrition-only authorities.

work.author: Gratian
work.description: The mid-twelfth-century canonical collection whose first-part distinctions open with the taxonomy of law received from Isidore and whose second part includes the Tractatus de poenitentia at C.33 q.3. First-part loci use d-N-pr for the dictum Gratiani opening a distinction and d-N-c-M for a chapter with any adjoining dicta. De poenitentia loci retain their full address as c-N-q-N-de-poenitentia-d-N, followed by c-M for a chapter or da-c-M/dp-c-M for a dictum before or after it; -ss-N or -ss-N-M bounds numbered sections. The Munich (MDZ) online transcription and page images of Friedberg's 1879 Leipzig edition serve as the accessible public-domain-based witnesses.
work.title: Decretum (Concordia discordantium canonum)
